nominees.name: Juan Maldacena
nominees.affiliation: Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton, USA

nominees.name: Edward Witten
nominees.affiliation: Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton, USA

motivation: Maldacena's 1997 conjecture that string theory in anti-de Sitter space is exactly equivalent to a conformal gauge theory on its boundary, made precise by Witten and by Gubser, Klebanov and Polyakov through the bulk-boundary dictionary, gave the first explicit, non-perturbative definition of quantum gravity. It turned the holographic principle into a working tool. It showed that black hole evaporation is unitary, and it produced the Ryu-Takayanagi relation between entanglement and geometry, which led to the current view of spacetime as emerging from quantum information. The duality also changed how physicists outside string theory work: it gave a way to handle strongly coupled matter, including the near-perfect fluidity of the quark-gluon plasma seen at RHIC and the LHC, strange metals, and quantum chaos bounds now probed on quantum simulators. Few ideas of the past thirty years have been taken up as widely across theoretical physics.
